comments.text: I'm 37 and own my home, car, have no debt and a 20k emergency fund. From my experience the only people that have it figured out are the ones who didn't listen to the conventional financial "wisdom" of the boomers and gen X. Debt is not a tool, there is no such thing as good debt, you do not have spend money to make money and there is no way to get rich quick unless your are EXTREMELY lucky. Hate to say it but we're in a new world and thinking outside the box is the only way. Me personally I worked full time at a call center and went to college full time to avoid debt after losing my scholarship after the first year. Everyone else pulled student loans. Never owned a credit card and instead built an emergency fund for when life happens. Everyone else, get a credit card for when life happens. Had a house with a mortgage and sold it and with the 3 years of equity I built a smaller house that was completely paid off. Now this one I give more understanding to because I grew around working class tradesmen and knew how to install AC units, drywall, plumbing and laying brick before I left high school. I drove my high school car for 14 years before buying a new one I saved the money for, CASH. Now this all started BECAUSE after college I spent 4 years living with my parents to save up money for my first down payment on a house and figuring out my plan. So feel no shame for moving back in but have a plan. Debt is the enemy. When you don't have a car payment, mortgage, student loan, credit card or payment plan you'll be shocked at how much money you have at the end of the month. I'm not a 6 figure guy but I eat out every day, fill up my tank, pay my utilities, insurance and taxes no problem and still have $2,500 left over to do with what I want. You and the Joneses are in debt and when the tide rolls out everyone sees yall skinny dipping. Your "wealth" is an illusion. The bank owns your house and car your biggest life purchases. Your furniture is rented, your material life is put on a credit card and your education was financed. I hope some of my thoughts help and realize that things have only gotten worse for young people but doubling down on life's bad decisions and caving to a system that just wants to churn out indentured servants is not the answer.
